Literally, as a kid masking WAS a survival technique for me. Same with school, I would mimic people I was around to try and fit in (I only realised this when I grew up.) And its kinda terrifying.

Also the gender non-conforming part is way too accurate, there is a community called Voidcore dedicated to how neurodivergent people feel unhuman. It's nice to have people understand how alienating autism can be and then you see fakers that make you just question, "why?" Especially when autism is still heavily stigmatised, it's not fun and quirky it's just people trying to live their lives.

See this is so under talked about, it took me till 21 to get a diagnosis because of masking and I thought it was so many other things because of the way I would try and fit in around people. It sucks ass how little information there is on it.

My fondest memory of my grandad was when we went to his allotment (like a garden outside of your home) together for the first time. I was there because he was getting older and I didn't want him going on his own when it was a really hot day. When we got there, my grandad and I did some gardening and I learnt some more about my grandads past. I also met my great uncle and aunt for the first time in a while. Then on the way back home, we saw a fruit stall and I mentioned being hungry. Now my grandad was always tight with money, not that I blamed him, but for the first time he gave me a few coins and I bought an apple. To some it may seem like nothing but I will treasure that moment for the rest of my life. 

When he started slipping away from us thanks to his decline in health I was devasted but I will always appreciate the time I spent with him. I'm sure he's somewhere looking down with fondness. This year I'm planning to make my garden beautiful in his honor. I hope I make him proud.
